How will the base price for ETFs be determined for the purpose of setting price bands, and what fallback prices apply if there is no trading in the last 30 minutes or no trade on T-1 day?
answer: Current position: the base price for determination of price bands of ETFs shall be T-1 day Closing Price. If there is no trading in the ETF during the last 30 minutes of T-1 day, then base price shall be the Last Traded Price (LTP) of the day. If there is no trade on T-1 day, then base price shall be the latest available closing NAV of the ETF.

query: For Equity and Debt ETFs (excluding Overnight and Liquid ETFs), what are the initial price band, how may it be flexed, and what are the cooling-off rules and limits on flexing?
repeat_answer:
Current position: For Equity and Debt ETFs (other than Overnight and Liquid ETFs) the initial price band is +10%.

It can be flexed up to +20% after a cooling-off period. The cooling-off period is 15 minutes after trades are executed at or above 9.90%, but if such trades occur during the last 30 minutes of trading the cooling-off period is 5 minutes. After the cooling-off the band may be flexed by 5% of the base price, for a maximum of two instances in one direction. The price band shall be flexed only in the direction of the price movement without corresponding adjustment on the opposite side.

query: overnight etfs liquid etfs auction close-out price determination
answer: Current position: The close-out price for Overnight ETFs and Liquid ETFs is the higher of two amounts. One is the highest price recorded in that ETF on the exchange in the settlement in which the concerned contract was entered into and up to the date of auction or close out. The other is 5% above the latest available closing price at the exchange on the day on which auction offers are called for.

query: How does SEBI circular 13804 set the base price for ETF price bands?
answer: Current position: the circular sets the base price as the T-1 day closing price — the last 30 minutes VWAP of the ETF. If there is no trading in the last 30 minutes of T-1 day, the base price is the Last Traded Price of that day. If there is no trade on T-1 day, the base price is the latest available closing NAV. The base price shall be adjusted for corporate actions. The circular also notes an implementation plan to move to T-1 day closing NAV as base price w.e.f. April 01, 2027.

query: Why can equity index funds only borrow for under-executed sell trades from August 2026 onwards?
answer: Current position: Equity‑oriented index funds may borrow for under‑executed sell trades only to participate in the Closing Auction Session, effective August 03, 2026. This follows because Regulation 42(1) permits mutual funds to borrow for settlement of trades by equity‑oriented index funds on account of under‑execution of sell trades. SEBI has clarified that such borrowings are permissible only for participation in the Closing Auction Session and tied that permission to the January 16, 2026 circular whose Closing Auction Session is effective August 03, 2026.

query: From what date were existing Angel Funds originally barred from taking money from non-accredited investors?
answer: Current position: the requirement now bars such Angel Funds from accepting contributions from non‑Accredited Investors after March 31, 2027. Originally, the bar was to take effect after September 08, 2026.

query: Before September 2026, which FPIs were exempt from furnishing investor group details?
answer: Before September 2026, FPIs that invested exclusively in Government Securities under the Fully Accessible Route were exempt from furnishing investor group details.

query: What were the financial result submission timelines for listed municipalities before the relaxation?
answer: Current position: Before the relaxation, listed municipalities had to submit half-yearly unaudited results within forty five days of the end of the first half year, and annual audited results within sixty days from the end of the financial year.

query: Can a cost accountant audit both investment advisers and research analysts?
answer: Yes. A member of the Institute of Cost Accountants of India can conduct the annual audit of Investment Advisers. A member of the Institute of Cost Accountants of India can conduct the annual audit of Research Analysts.
